assumptions_and_limits: C128 per-class GB/s from node a1 commit 15fd7f4 are assumed to hold on the C256 point; a1 reference 5162 tok/s is branch-recorded, not re-measured here.
Mean decode seq 288.5 assumes the 512 output tokens are uniformly spread; the sliding-window clamp does not bind below seq 512.
'other' kernels are scaled linearly 128->256 with a +/-30% band.
The anchor is a whole-run aggregate (includes 2% prefill and any tail/queueing); the prediction is a steady-state per-forward band.

falsifiable_discriminator.additional_readouts: cudaGraphLaunch count per forward (does bs=256 replay a graph under --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64?), actual batch label, per-class effective GB/s.
falsifiable_discriminator.if_measured_per_forward_ms_in_prediction: the C128 trace's per-byte efficiencies transfer to C256; the anchor comparison is not like-for-like (different run conditions or an unmodelled wall-time term) and there is no C256 kernel bottleneck to chase.
falsifiable_discriminator.if_measured_per_forward_ms_is_45_to_52: the ~10-13 ms excess is real at bs=256; attribute it by kernel class from the same trace (attention vs GEMM vs other vs host gaps / eager-vs-graph) before proposing any patch.
